description: Bounded primary-source starting register. Facts, historical status, interpretation and recheck needs are separate; no claim of exhaustive current legal coverage.

events.applicable_scope: New Jersey internet casino and online sportsbook operations; company exposure is not quantified.
events.observed_fact: P.L. 2025, c.66 establishes a 19.75% base tax on internet casino gaming revenue and online sports wagering revenue, effective July 1, 2025.
events.accounting_effect: Base rate 19.75%; the Act also retains separate investment-alternative and additional sports-wagering provisions. This is not an all-in effective tax rate.
events.business_interpretation: Analyst inference: higher gaming taxes can pressure operator economics even when market revenue grows. July 2025 effectiveness makes this existing context for July 2026 versus July 2025, not a newly dated September 2026 deterioration.
events.limitations: Enacted text retained, not a complete audit of subsequent amendments or current company tax accounting. No company EBITDA or valuation change is calculated.
events.next_check: Review current NJ tax guidance and issuer disclosures before quantifying a company effect.
events.source_locator: Sections 1 and 2; effective date in section 4; approval date at end.

events.applicable_scope: Illinois master licensees taking online/mobile sports wagers; company-specific wager counts and incidence are not established.
events.observed_fact: The Illinois Gaming Board 2025 Annual Report describes P.A. 104-0006 adding a per-wager tax from July 1, 2025: $0.25 on the first 20 million wagers per licensee and $0.50 above that threshold. The report records collections during July-December 2025.
events.accounting_effect: Per-wager dollar charge, not a percentage of handle or gross revenue. Aggregate handle cannot determine its company cost.
events.business_interpretation: Analyst inference: cost per transaction and any operator response may change the economics of smaller wagers. Treat this as existing statutory context; do not attribute current volume changes to the tax without further evidence.
events.limitations: The retained annual report establishes the reported 2025 rule and collections, not a full September 2026 amendment or company pass-through review. Exact report publication date is unknown.
events.next_check: Recheck current Illinois statute/regulator guidance and operator disclosures, then obtain wager counts if estimating cost.
events.source_locator: Physical/printed page 15, Legislation 2025, Sports Wagering, Per Wager Tax.

events.applicable_scope: Kalshi sports-event-contract litigation against Nevada officials; named tickers are research exposures, not parties or automatic beneficiaries.
events.observed_fact: In KalshiEX v. Assad, No. 25-7516, the Ninth Circuit affirmed dissolution of preliminary protection against Nevada enforcement on sports-event contracts and remanded the election-contract issue. Kalshi had not established likely success on its preemption theory at this stage.
events.accounting_effect: Not quantified; no observed company revenue, margin or cost change follows mechanically from the disposition.
events.business_interpretation: Analyst inference: the ruling is relevant to competition between licensed sportsbooks and prediction products. Effects may differ for incumbent sportsbook operations and those companies own prediction-market initiatives.
events.limitations: Published disposition of a preliminary-injunction appeal, not a nationwide final ban or a measured fundamentals improvement. Subsequent rehearing, stay, mandate and other-circuit status are not established by this PDF.
events.next_check: Check subsequent court orders and relevant dockets before treating the August 28 posture as current; retain competing legal outcomes separately.
events.source_locator: Opinion physical page 47, section IV disposition; filing date on physical page 2.
